title: The measuring legend says something useful now that Size and Gap share one colour
goal: While the Measure tool is on, a small key in the corner of the picture lists Size and Spacing with a colour swatch each. Since every measurement now starts in the same blue, both rows show the same swatch, so the key no longer tells them apart. Decide with the user whether the key goes, tells the roles apart some other way, or stays.
notes: Follows every-measurement-shares-one-remembered-look-blu (2026-10-13): MeasureStyles keeps ONE colour set for every role, so measureLegendEntries (EditorState+Measure.swift, near the end) lists Size and Spacing each swatched in its top-most measurement ink, which is now the same #3774D5 by default. The legend is behind next-measure-roles (on at Next defaults); legend-corner-slots walk covers its placement. The redline mock (docs/design/mocks/pages/redline.html) draws Size red and Spacing blue with this legend; the user overrode the colour split on 2026-10-13 ("gap vs size shouldn't be different").
acceptance: A decision card offers the user what the key should do now that Size and Spacing share one look, with keep, drop and a different marker as options, and drop marked as the recommendation if the key no longer earns its corner
Whatever the user picks is built and a walk at Next defaults shows the key (or its absence) with a Size and a Gap on the picture
No two rows of the key ever show identical swatches with nothing else telling them apart
